label: complementary
rationale: The predicate 'eggs_fetched' in FOUR_NP relates to an action of fetching eggs, while 'on_list' in NAUG relates to an action of crossing out an entity from a list. The 'eggs_fetched' predicate describes a state (eggs have been fetched), whereas 'on_list' describes a state of presence on a list. They represent different aspects of the same scenario - the eggs being fetched and the thief being tracked. One describes an action, the other a state related to tracking. The action contexts for 'eggs_fetched' involve an entity ('t') being fetched, while the action context for 'on_list' involves an entity ('c') being crossed out. The parameters of both predicates are identical ('entity'), but their usages and associated actions are distinct. The 'crossed_out' effect of 'cross_out_comet' directly negates the 'on_list' predicate, demonstrating a complementary relationship. The 'burn_ed' precondition of 'cross_out_comet' is unrelated to the 'eggs_fetched' predicate. The two predicates describe different aspects of the same situation, one describing the action of fetching eggs and the other describing the state of an entity being tracked. The 'brother_thief' parameter in the 'shoot_eggs' action context is irrelevant to the 'on_list' predicate. The 'eggs_fetched' predicate is used to describe the state of the eggs being fetched, while the 'on_list' predicate is used to describe the state of an entity being tracked. The two predicates are complementary because they describe different aspects of the same situation.
